commonSettings.label: Idle session timeout (seconds)
commonSettings.description: How long a chat session stays warm after its last request before it is closed. 0 keeps it until the agent stops.

commonSettings.label: Idle agent shutdown (minutes)
commonSettings.description: Stop the agent process after this many idle minutes. 0 never stops it. It starts again on the next request.

commonSettings.label: Dump requests (debug)
commonSettings.description: Write each request a client sends to a JSON file in the agent's folder on the server. The files hold the whole prompt, so keep this off unless you are debugging.

settings.label: Auth preference
settings.description: Which credentials the Claude agent uses when both an API key and a signed-in account (OAuth) are available. Changing it restarts the agent.
optionDescriptions: Use the saved API key when there is one, otherwise the signed-in account.
Use the saved API key. Without one, the agent falls back to its signed-in account.
Always use the signed-in account and ignore the saved API key and the key environment variables.

settings.label: Tool search
settings.description: Whether the client's tools are loaded on demand. On: the model sees only tool names and fetches a tool's description when it needs it, which makes each request much smaller but can add a lookup step before a tool is first used (not supported by every model, Haiku included). Off: every tool's full description is sent with every request. Default: the agent decides. Changing it restarts the agent.
optionDescriptions: Leave it to the agent.
Load tools on demand.
Send every tool's description with every request.

settings.label: Default thinking effort
settings.description: The thinking effort for a request that names none, such as a subagent, or that asks for Default. Default leaves it to the agent, which can choose the most expensive level. A level the model does not offer is ignored.
optionDescriptions: Leave it to the agent.
Minimal reasoning for the fastest answers.
Balanced reasoning for everyday tasks.
Deeper reasoning for involved tasks.
Extended reasoning for difficult tasks.
Maximum reasoning; the slowest and most expensive choice.

settings.label: Show thinking text
settings.description: On: the response carries a summary of Claude's reasoning as thinking text. Off: it carries none, as when Claude leaves it out of the stream. The model thinks and the tokens are billed the same either way. Changing it restarts the agent.

settings.label: Replace the Claude Code system prompt
settings.description: On: Claude's built-in Claude Code prompt is replaced by the system prompt the client sends for the chat. Off: the client's prompt is added to the end of the Claude Code prompt. Changing it restarts the agent.

settings.label: Max live chat sessions
settings.description: How many chats may keep a live Claude process at once. Each live chat holds its own process of about 100-200 MB; past this number the least recently used idle chat is closed and its next message resumes it from disk, which is slower and misses the prompt cache. Minimum 1.

settings.label: Auth preference
settings.description: Which credentials the Codex agent uses when both an OpenAI API key and a ChatGPT account are available. Changing it restarts the agent.
optionDescriptions: Use the saved OpenAI API key when there is one, otherwise the ChatGPT account.
Use the saved OpenAI API key. Without one, the agent falls back to its ChatGPT account.
Always use the ChatGPT account: the saved API key is ignored and CODEX_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY are withheld from the agent.

settings.label: Largest context window
settings.description: Ask Codex for the largest context window each model allows instead of its default. Models that cannot be raised keep their default. A larger window delays compaction, so long chats re-send more history on every turn and use up your plan limits faster. Changing it restarts the agent.

settings.label: Default thinking effort
settings.description: The thinking effort for a request that names none, such as a subagent. Default leaves it to the agent. An effort a request names is always kept, and a level the model does not offer is ignored.
optionDescriptions: Leave it to the agent.
Minimal reasoning for the fastest answers.
Balanced reasoning for everyday tasks.
Deeper reasoning for involved tasks.
Extended reasoning for difficult tasks.
Maximum reasoning.
Beyond Max; the slowest and most expensive choice.

settings.label: Replace the Codex system prompt
settings.description: On: Codex's built-in instructions, bundled skills and environment notes are replaced by a one-line base identity, with the client's system prompt for the chat after it. Off: the client's prompt is added to Codex's own instructions. Changing it restarts the agent.

settings.label: Default thinking effort
settings.description: The thinking effort for a request that names none, such as a subagent. Default leaves it to the agent. An effort a request names is always kept, and a level the model does not offer is ignored.
optionDescriptions: Leave it to the agent.
Minimal reasoning for the fastest answers.
Balanced reasoning for everyday tasks.
Deeper reasoning for involved tasks.

settings.label: Replace the Antigravity system prompt
settings.description: On: the chat's agent takes a neutral base identity instead of Antigravity's persona, with the client's system prompt for the chat after it. Off: it keeps a short Antigravity persona, with the same prompt after it. Antigravity's own generated prompt is replaced either way; its sections about skills, artifacts and messaging stay. Warning: Google answers a prompt it does not accept with a 429 (Resource exhausted) on every request; if chats fail that way with this on, turn it off. Changing it restarts the agent.

settings.label: Auth preference
settings.description: Which credentials the agent uses when both a Gemini API key and a signed-in account are available. Changing it restarts the agent.
optionDescriptions: Use the saved API key when there is one, otherwise the signed-in account.
Use the saved API key. Without one, the agent falls back to its signed-in account.
Always use the signed-in account and ignore the saved API key and the key environment variables.
